material_findings.statement: Governed erasure performs irreversible external deletion before durable completion of the database-side governance record.
material_findings.authority_basis: FIBC-009 FC clause: 'erasure cannot be declared complete unless every identified payload/derivative was treated.' FIBC-009: 'A conflict with an immutable artifact yields erasure_partial/erasure_blocked and escalation -- never a false erasure_complete.' FIBC-009: 'Produces an evidence_tombstone preserving identity, version, actor, date, reason, and structural references.' FIBDB-043: 'erasure_state only advances forward, never regresses from erasure_complete.'
material_findings.independent_verification: Measured at lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:902-971: supabase.storage.remove() executes the irreversible object deletion, then updateCurrentEvidenceVersion sets the terminal erasure_state, then the evidenceTombstones row is inserted. No durable governance state is written between the permission check and the destructive act -- erasure_state is never set to erasure_requested or erasure_in_progress before deletion, and the pre-act record is an audit event, not the governed tombstone. A failure after storage removal and before the tombstone insert yields erased content with no tombstone.

material_findings.statement: Governed erasure currently processes only the latest evidence version, while FIBC-009 refers to derived versions.
material_findings.authority_basis: FIBC-009 verbatim: 'Erases every Uellix-controlled derivative -- stored object, persisted text, derived versions, OCR, thumbnails, chunks, embeddings, search indices, caches.' FIBIU-07 SERVICE_CHANGES repeats 'sweeps every Uellix-controlled derivative -- stored object, persisted text, derived versions, OCR, thumbnails, chunks, embeddings, indices, caches.'
material_findings.independent_verification: Measured at lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:911 getLatestEvidenceVersion(evidenceId) resolves a single version, and line 941 updateCurrentEvidenceVersion nulls content on the current version only. Persisted content on prior/superseded evidence_versions rows is not swept. The docs/19 grounding-derivative clause is separately satisfied vacuously and is not the defect.

ag_w2_b1_1_adjudication.question: Does FIBIU-05's FILES_OR_DOMAINS enumeration exhaustively bound the FIBC-007 exposure filter, or is the controlling FIBC-007 safety property plus FIBIU-05's EXIT_GATE broader than that list?
ag_w2_b1_1_adjudication.frozen_interpretation: FILES_OR_DOMAINS is an implementation locator and minimum expected surface list. It is NOT an exhaustive waiver from the controlling FIBC-007 safety property or from FIBIU-05's EXIT_GATE. Where the enumerated list and the exit gate differ, the contract safety invariant and the exit gate control.
evidence_from_sealed_record: FIBIU-05's own SERVICE_CHANGES field requires 'an exposure filter across every output surface -- report, annex, export, public surface, and Stella context'. The universal quantifier is internal to the same unit that carries the narrower file list, so the narrow reading contradicts the unit against itself, not merely against FIBC-007.
FIBIU-05's own EXIT_GATE requires that 'no output surface exposes classified content'. An exit gate stated over all output surfaces cannot be satisfied by filtering a subset of them.
FIBC-007 states the governed exposure domains as a closed list of five kinds -- reports, annexes, exports, public surfaces, and Stella context -- not as a list of files.

FIBIU-05's FILES_OR_DOMAINS entries include line ranges (lib/reports/public-verify.ts:67-70, lib/stella/context/build-advisor-context.ts:191). A line-range entry is a pointer to a known defect site; it is a locator idiom and cannot coherently be read as a scope boundary, since a safety property is not confined to four lines of a file.

Independent corroboration from the derived layer: the W2 execution mapping's B1 authorized_surface omits lib/reports/public-verify.ts and lib/stella/context/build-advisor-context.ts entirely, although FIBIU-05 explicitly names both. A surface enumeration that omits paths its own sealed unit names is demonstrably non-exhaustive, which independently defeats the exhaustive-waiver reading at the derived layer as well.
explicit_limits: This does NOT create permission to edit arbitrary repository files.
Implementation may touch only additional concrete exposure surfaces demonstrably required to satisfy FIBC-007.
The remediation implementer MUST enumerate each added path and state its causal relation to the contract.
No sensitivity classification may be inferred. Automatic detection may recommend but never declare non-sensitive (FIBC-007).
Evidence must NOT be blindly hidden from authorized internal users where the contract permits retention.
ag_w2_b1_1_adjudication.fail_closed_rule: Any content sent to external model context, public output, report annex, or export MUST fail closed under the exact sensitivity contract.

Public surface named directly in FIBIU-05 FILES_OR_DOMAINS; the exposure filter was materialized here in B1. Remediation must not regress it. FIBIU-26 consumes the same precedence ('V-26 classification has absolute precedence, evaluated fail-closed before activation or modification').

R-B1-05.title: ERASURE DURABILITY / DERIVED VERSIONS

frozen_rules.statement: No irreversible content deletion may happen before sufficient durable governance state exists to avoid an erased-with-no-tombstone outcome.
frozen_rules.authority_basis: FIBC-009 requires the operation to produce an evidence_tombstone preserving identity, version, actor, date, reason and structural references, and declares operational states erasure_requested|erasure_in_progress|erasure_complete|erasure_partial|erasure_blocked. FIBDB-043 constrains erasure_state to advance forward only. A vocabulary that begins at erasure_requested and passes through erasure_in_progress is ordered with respect to the destructive act; the destructive act cannot precede the state that represents having requested it.

frozen_rules.statement: Storage/database partial failure must produce an explicit governed non-complete state.
frozen_rules.authority_basis: FIBC-009: 'A conflict with an immutable artifact yields erasure_partial/erasure_blocked and escalation.' FIBC-009 FC clause: 'erasure cannot be declared complete unless every identified payload/derivative was treated.'

frozen_rules.statement: A partial operation must never be represented as completed.
Erasure must account for every evidence version and derived version in scope under FIBC-009, not silently only the latest, where such versions exist.
frozen_rules.authority_basis: FIBC-009 verbatim: 'Erases every Uellix-controlled derivative -- stored object, persisted text, derived versions, OCR, thumbnails, chunks, embeddings, search indices, caches.' Where such versions do not exist the clause is satisfied vacuously, exactly as FIBC-009 already provides for docs/19 grounding derivatives ('if grounding derivatives do not exist for an evidence item, none are created; if they exist, they must participate before erasure_complete').

FIBDB-032 BACKFILL_CLASS: 'SCHEMA_ONLY, behavioral -- hardening stage E only.' FIBDB-033 BACKFILL_CLASS: 'SCHEMA_ONLY, behavioral -- must ship together with FIBDB-032 ... hardening stage E.' W2_EXECUTION_MAPPING B1 expected_output: 'FIBDB-005/037/043/014/031 materialized; 032/033 deferred to stage E.'

R-B1-05.early_activation_additional_hazard: FIBDB-033 states the pair must ship together: 'revoking privilege without the trigger leaves a privilege-error path with no guidance; the trigger without the revoke leaves the silent 0-row path open.' Activating either alone in Stage A would create a defect authority already anticipated.

authority_gap_assessment.basis: The frozen Stage-A schema CAN safely represent durable request / partial / completed sequencing without new authority. FIBDB-043 already provides all five erasure_state values on evidence_versions, including erasure_requested and erasure_in_progress. db/schema.ts records the intended split directly: 'Transient progress (erasure_requested/erasure_in_progress) lives on evidence_versions.erasure_state; this table records only the terminal state (erasure_complete/erasure_partial/erasure_blocked) an erasure actually reached.' No new workflow needs to be invented and no authority gap is reported.

One negative control per governed output path; a single shared control does not satisfy this.

Sensitive evidence must not enter Stella context by the mere fact of being linked to the project (FIBIU-05 STELLA_CHANGES). Existing PII redaction at the provider boundary must be shown preserved, not replaced.

No sensitivity classification may be inferred: an automatic detector must never be able to drive a version to non_sensitive. Approval must remain impossible without an explicit human classification (EVIDENCE_SENSITIVITY_UNEVALUATED).
PRIMARY RUN-BINDING CONTROL: a sufficiency determination recorded for run R1 with outcome O MUST NOT satisfy approval of run R2 with the same outcome O.

None of the following may substitute for the correct explicit run-bound human determination: an old or superseded determination; a large number of evidence rows; a high confidence_score. Sufficiency is never inferred from count, individual status, confidence_score, or Stella (FIBC-008).

An induced failure of the storage removal, and an induced failure of the database write, must each leave an explicit governed non-complete state and must never yield erased content with no durable governance record, nor a false erasure_complete.

Multiple evidence versions: an evidence item with more than one version must have every in-scope version treated, or the operation must block explicitly and safely. Silent latest-only treatment must fail the control.
contentHashPreserved must be false when no hash value is preserved (including the FIBIU-04 legacy_content_unverifiable case), and must never be hardcoded.
Every evidence_tombstone audit event's entityId must denote the entity its entityType names.

Each governed action must be denied server-side for a role below its FIBIU-29 permission floor -- canClassifyEvidenceSensitivity (impact_manager+), canDetermineEvidenceSufficiency (impact_manager+), canEraseEvidenceContent (organization_admin+) -- with no client-side authorization and no service_role client on a user path.

The governance/baseline assertions must remain genuinely falsifiable after re-derivation: a deliberate corpus mutation must still fail them. Re-derivation must not convert an assertion into a tautology.
